instagram.author: techinsixty
instagram.body:
Comment " Tool " for link

Commitment Issues analyzes your GitHub repository activity and turns inactive projects into a humorous “death certificate.” It detects when development stopped, captures the last commit, and presents everything in a clean, shareable format.

Key Features
▪︎ Analyze any public GitHub repository
▪︎ Detect inactivity and last commit date
▪︎ Generate “death certificate” summary
▪︎ Auto-fill project details
▪︎ Funny cause of death generation
▪︎ Shareable output

Tool creator: @dotsystemsdevs
this tool declares a death certificate for your GitHub repos

instagram.author: parth.builds
instagram.body:
You think you’ve used GitHub a lot… but have you really used it?
Comment “Repo” for the repository link.

Most people just browse projects for 5–10 minutes and move on.
“You notice a bug, UI issue, or a missing feature… and just scroll away.”

That’s exactly where GitHub Issues comes in.

Instead of ignoring it → drop an issue.
That’s how real open source starts.
And if you go one step further → you can fix it with a pull request.

Small observation → real impact → actual contribution. 

(coding, college life, hackathon, engineering, engineer life, student, projects, trending, parth narkar, parth builds, GitHub, claude, vercel, deployment)
Bahot time se GitHub use kar rahe ho lekin kabhi ISSUES create kiye hai? Issues? GitHub ka kuch issue hai kya? Abey chup. Aap ek kisi website par ho aur aapko kuch UI mein error aaya. Button theek se kaam nahi kiya. Aapko laga ki yeh feature iss website mein hona chahiye. And aise bahot saare bugs and improvements. Toh isi cheez ke liye we use GitHub Issues. Just go to this repository, test the website for 5 to 10 minutes and kuch issue laga toh Create kar dena. Issues mein aao, Create new issue. Add title, description, labels, click on Create. Then you have successfully created your GitHub issue. Just comment "REPO" for getting the repository link and share this reel with your friends and follow karlena for knowing each and everything about coding. Bye bye.
